correctness.rationale: The valuation argument proves precisely the allowed palindrome centers and confirms every possible suffix is represented; low-bit complement alters only one run-boundary XOR term. Strong induction gives optimal predecessors and the factorial recurrence. Transition-set counting yields the exact binomial histogram. Independent palindrome-center expansion for all 65535 prefixes and large-number bit identities corroborates the unrestricted proof; no finite bound is used as a substitute for induction.

originality.rationale: Inspected exact Zimin suffix characterization (Fici et al. 2014) and exact minimum-length theorem (Li 2020); neither provides a count or distribution of distinct minimum-cut chains. The additional local optimal-suffix classification and multiplicative recurrence give the stated factorial law. OEIS A010551 lists factorial values under other interpretations; no claim is made that the integer sequence itself is new. Targeted discovery searches found no equivalence, with acknowledged residual risk.
residual_risks: Earlier unindexed or differently worded results could already give the factorial multiplicity under a shortest-path or mask-operation interpretation.

General-purpose algorithms can enumerate shortest decompositions for a given finite word; novelty concerns the explicit all-index theorem and dyadic distribution, not computability or a new integer sequence.

value.rationale: A natural previously unknown quantity—number of optimal palindromic cut chains for the standard Zimin extremal family—is solved for every index. Factorial dependence on binary-run count, complete classification of valid last cuts, and exact binomial distribution supply substantial structural information not determined by the known minimum-length formula. The abstract factorial sequence is known; the significance is its exact Zimin-factorization interpretation.
